title: Why subtle tweaks get drowned out: focus on the big, in-your-face effects
summary: Jason Cohen argues the "butterfly effect" idea in marketing, where tiny design or psychological nudges drive big results, is mostly noise. In a world of competing stimuli, subtle influences cancel out, so effort should go to large, obvious levers like a popular blogger's mention, a spreadable story, or thrilling one customer.

principles.text: Subtle influences cancel out amid constant ambient stimuli, so don't build strategy on them.
principles.quote: If I'm constantly influenced in all directions, the forces cancel each other out, and none of them matter.

principles.text: Spend time on big, obvious, non-subliminal effects instead of chasing tiny psychological tricks.
principles.quote: instead of chasing subtle subliminal effects, most of which will be wiped away by the ambient noise of life, we could spend our time on the big-ass, in-yo-face, non-subliminal effects.

principles.text: A mention from a popular blogger beats cosmetic tweaks like logo color.
principles.quote: if you get a popular blogger to mention you, that's more influential than the color of your logo.

principles.text: A story people want to spread outweighs polish like a snappy home-page animation.
principles.quote: if you have a compelling story that people intrinsically want to spread, that's more influential than building a snappy animation for your home page.

principles.text: Thrilling one real prospect in a demo is worth more than thousands of branded website hits.
principles.quote: if you thoroughly thrill one person in a product demo, that's more money in the bank than 1,000 people hitting your website and getting "branded" that you're "trustworthy" because of your steel-blue color palette and stoic font.

principles.text: Most of our small-detail efforts are drowned out by the distraction of the internet and life; take care of the big stuff.
principles.quote: I just think most of our efforts are drowned out by the seething distraction that is the internet and life in general.
